blocks.text: When we come to History in the Montessori approach for elementary children we can see how the aim of the education is always the development of the child and therefore the subjects are presented to support this aim – history tries to build human solidarity. A very different approach from the national curriculum which it seems that it is concentrated on the moments of tension between humanity.

If someone would arrive from a different planet and see that after more than 2.5 million years of humanity all we present in schools to the children are the moments when different groups of people had different opinions and fought about it, this person from another planet would think that we want to educate a future warrior, a biased person and someone who would bring back all these old conflicts to justify the present.
However, if we take a different approach and through the study of history we present a story of human solidarity, a story of the “human work” for development and a story
f cooperation chances are that the new human being is going to love the world,
appreciate humanity and protect it from any harm by being first a trustworthy member of the society.

“[…] traditional history was often a very pessimistic kind of story, a very pessimistic presentation of humanity. To illustrate this point of view, I want to give you a quote from Edward Gibbon, the English historian who wrote the famous work The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire: “History is indeed little more than the register of the
crimes, follies, and misfortunes of mankind”” – Baiba Krumins Grazzini – History: Human solidarity: Man Whither Bound

With the Montessori approach to history everything changes, the span of time studied, the focus and the content. The approach of the history is optimistic and makes the child love humanity, understand its struggles but also the great work. It is important, especially for the young elementary children, to have this optimistic welcome in the human history where we present to them the good of the humanity.

Dr. Montessori does not start with civilization, she deals with all humanity and going even further stating that history starts from the very, very beginning. The history is presented with stories of truth and even if we can think of “God Who Has No Hands” as opening the subject of geography but it is also the starting point of history, the history of the Universe.

As the work with the Montessori approach has the development of the child at the center, by offering history in this manner we help the child to feel part of the universe, part of life and part of all humanity. If in the traditional approach to history the heroes are always the kings, princes or princesses, war veterans and so on, with the Montessori approach the heroes are all the human beings. That means not only the famous, powerful but also the ordinary human beings which through their work
took us from the life in the open wild to the life we live today. We can therefore see the history as a long story of human work.

We want to help the children to think about the human life in the past, to imagine the life as it was with all its benefits and hardships. The use of imagination is one of the sensitivities of the children in the second plane of development, this means that they not only have the capacity but they are also enjoying the stories and the exploration of what it can be perceived only with the eyes of the mind.
For the work in history there are three keys: fundamental human needs, migration and time.

The fundamental human needs help the children understand that we all share the same needs, we are all bonded in this way. It is a beautiful way in which the children can put the diversity and differences into perspective. Having a good understanding of the fundamental human needs help the children to explore the history from a different perspective allowing them to discover how we satisfied these needs in our more than 2.5 million years of existence.

The work with migration is very important as it brings a new vision in how the humanity developed, especially today when the topic is so debated in mass media. The human beings have been always on the move, they mixed and shared their knowledge, discoveries and inventions. It is impressive to see what it would’ve meant for humanity to live in isolation – each group by its own in the same place. The children can explore all the faces of humanity, the good decisions and the bad decisions that we might have taken during our history. It brings such a different perspective when you are free to explore, to investigate and to see that the human history is a biased story depending on who is the story teller. It allows the children to grow as critical thinkers, open to appreciate the human mind, the love and the hands as an instrument of the mind.

The third key is the time. When we think about history it is impossible not to think about time. The history is embedded in a matrix of time. Everything that we think that is fixed and constant, if you look at it over a long enough span of time, actually changes (E.g. the tilt of the Earth, the length of the day). Nothing remains the same and this important for the children to explore, as they might find it hard to imagine. With the help of the imagination, the materials and the stories the children can picture realities that are long gone.

If we guide the children’s exploration in the correct way they might grow and develop a deep love for humanity – human solidarity. A love that will help them avoid many of the mistakes that we have done in the past but not because they are aware of each and every cruelty ever committed but because this love gives way for empathy, care and understanding that despite all our differences we are one:
La nazione unica.
This fable it is connected with the first fable “The god without hands” and it starts by referring to the elements: sun, air, water and land.
Timeline of life
Cosmic fable

Today we are going to hear a story: The Story of Life. Do you remember the story of how the Earth came to be? Well today we have the story of the coming of life, the plants, the animals, human beings. But first think back now to when the Earth was born. What was the earth like when it was born? A little drop of light and heat of commotion and confusion. Yet in this tiny drop every particle had been given its set of laws. So when the Earth cooled, everything settled down according to those laws, the rocks, the water, the air. From afar the Earth looked like a beautiful little cloud and when the sun looked at her he couldn’t stop looking, he looked day and night, because she was so beautiful. Then one day the sun saw that something was not quite right, not quite in order. It had rained a lot on Earth and as the water passed through the air it got mixed up with a gas (carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, and nitrous oxide). Gas and water were washing away the rocks and filling the seas full of salt. (Mineral salts).

There were also many storms and then the water pounded away against the rocks, breaking them up, shattering them and they were falling into the seas. The seas were filling up more and more and the land was being washed away. It looked as though the order that was created at the beginning was breaking down.
Who was causing this? Who was the culprit?
Sun looked at Water and said: "Water, you must be the culprit. You are washing the salts into the sea!"

But the Water said: "Who, me? What have I done? Remember how I am made and the laws that I must follow! When I become hot I disappear, but if I get cold I fall (rain falling) and if I find a hollow, and then being a liquid, I have to flow into it. I don't have any choice! And my sister Air stirs me up and carries me around, dropping me on the rocks. It's her fault that I have to move, talk to her!"

The Air said: "Me? I was given the job of covering the Earth with layers of blankets so she won't be cold. I have to always cover her, but she has a big tummy and her head and feet are frozen. I have to keep on the move to cover them. Whenever I go near Water, she jumps on my back to take a ride! That's fine when it's flat, but when I run into mountains it's different. It is hard climbing mountains and I get so tired carrying Water up the mountain so I have to drop her. I can't play all of the time. I have important work to do! It's the fault of those rocks! Why does the Earth have to have such a wrinkly skin? Rocks have no consideration at all! They do not move to let me pass. Sometimes they get so hot that when I go near them I have to climb up to avoid burning. When they are freezing, I cringe!"

The Rocks said with one voice: "Why do you blame us? We are not doing anything but sitting around! Do you think we want to get hot? The sun shines on us and we cannot help it. We are made this way. If you ask us, Sun, it is your fault. You are the culprit!"

And so it went on. No one wanted to be blamed, but the trouble just got worse and worse. You see, everything was at fault. Everything was acting just the way it should, following its own laws, and yet the beautiful order was being threatened. Soon the Earth would no longer be a beautiful pearl in space. Something had to be done. But what could be done?

A wonderful thing happened! Something new was created, things so small that you could not see them. These tiny drops of a jelly-like substance were given a set of laws that would save the Earth. In order to exist, these tiny jelly drops had to eat, grow and create others like themselves. And so life came like this, as tiny chops of jelly in the water.

These tiny chops of jelly began to eat and eat and eat, and they began to clean up the sea by eating the salts in the water. From the salts, some built shells around their bodies for protection. When they died, their shells dropped to the floor of the sea with the salts trapped in them. Time passed and layer upon layer of these tiny shells built up mixed up and created an ooze like a mud. They were like the pages of a book. Some of these pages remained that were laid down long before we were born, were left for us to read to tell us what happened long, long ago.

Now these tiny creatures were made of just one tiny cell. You have to imagine that you are made up of billions of cells. This tiny cell did all the work that needed to be done - all the eating, breathing, growing, and getting rid of what the cell did not want. These tiny creatures drifted around the seas, cleaning the waters for a long time.

As time went by some of these creatures seem to have said, "Let's join together and be a bigger creature. We could do things better that way." Thus, they formed into bigger creatures made of many cells. They grew, multiplied and fed in the sea as they drifted about.

Then, some of the creatures thought, "Instead of each cell doing the same thing, it would be much better if some of us did one job and others did other jobs. Some could do the eating, some could do the breathing, and some could do the moving, and so
n." So the cells divided the work up amongst themselves. Some cells were to do the

eating, others were to do the moving, and others would do the breathing. Thus came creatures with legs, mouths, hearts, lungs, and so on - creatures with organs. When the Book of the Earth opens up for us on the first page, we can see that all of these creatures were already there. The tiny one-celled creatures, the multi-celled creatures, and those with different organs.
(Open up the Time Line of Life to the Cambrian Period)
When the Book of Earth opened up its first page, all these tiny creatures were already there, living in the water. Here is one creature, a one-celled creature with no shell. (point to the amoeba)

Here's another, with two little whips to help it move about. (point to the flagellate) This creature is made of a group of cells. (point to the sponge) Sea anemones like this (point to the sea anemone) stayed in one place. In order to get food, they moved the water with these long thin body parts so tiny creatures in the water would come into their mouths. There was one kind of creature that could be found in these ancient seas in great numbers. (point to the trilobites) They are known as trilobites, a little bit like our lobsters. Trilobites were the most advanced creatures of their time, and they grew in many shapes and sizes. Today we no longer have these creatures, but they were around for a long time at the beginning of life on Earth.
(Open up the Time Line of Life to the Ordovician Period)
Time went on and all kinds of creatures appeared, and all sorts of experiments went
n. Look here at this creature! (point to the cephalopod) It had its legs attached to its
head. (Open up the Time Line of Life to the Silurian Period)
As time went on, all kinds of animals appeared. Here we have some that look like flowers on a stalk. (point to the crinoids)

They stayed in one place like the anemones. Some built rings of stone out of the salts in the in the seawater. These rings held their soft jelly-like bodies. With the feathery parts, they moved in the water they could catch tiny creatures floating about in the sea. Because they were so colourful and looked like flowers, they were called sea lilies. (point to the seal lilies) But they were animals, not plants. When they died, the stalk of rings collapsed and fell to the bottom of the sea. The waters were full of life at this time!
(Open up the Time Line of Life to the Silurian & Devonian Period)
There were creatures of long ago who, instead of eating other creatures, made their
wn food out of sunlight and salts in the water. As they drifted about, they thought, "I

wonder what it would be like over there on the land?" Therefore, they drifted over to the edge of the sea, the waves and tides caught some and washed them onto the land. They stayed there until the water caught them again and washed them back into the sea. They day came, however, when some said, "Oh, it is lovely here!" They stayed on the land because they had plenty of sunshine and air, which contained a gas that they needed to make food. They attached themselves to the land, from which they could get water and salts. (point to the Silurian/Devonian marsh plants) And so came the plants. For the first time, plants appeared on the land! When the plants died, they left their bodies there, preparing the ground for other life forms to come.
(Open up the Time Line of Life to the Devonian Period)

Life was now moving onto the land. While plants were trying out the land, two new kinds of creatures appeared. One of these helped to build up the land by eating salts in the sea. The other was an animal that had a hard rod in its body. Up until now, the hard part was always outside the body. This was the beginning of animals with backbones. This animal eventually developed into the fish, but these fish were different from those we have today. They were enormous fish with hard plates on the
utside to protect themselves. (point to the Devonian, armoured, jawless fish)

They buried themselves in the bottom of the sea with only hard plates sticking out, and waited until a bit of dinner floated by, and then they would open up their mouths and gobble it up. Some could swim very swiftly, and they developed movable fins which helped them to swim better.
(Open up the Time Line of Life to the Carboniferous Period)

Then the land began to rise. Places that were in the sea became land and places that had no rain began to dry out. Some fish were cut off from the water. Imagine being a creature in one of these places! You need water so that you can live, but the water dries up! Fish, who needed water, began to think about what to do now that they were on land. They had to change or die. So they decided to build a sack inside their body with water in it so that when there was no water they could still breathe. And so the secret of breathing outside of water was invented.
And so came the amphibians, animals who live partly in the water. (point to the Carboniferous amphibians)
Fins were of no use any more, so they changed and became legs to walk on. So animals like salamanders and the frogs appeared (point to the salamanders and frogs)

Something very wonderful happened when the amphibians came. The sound of the first voice on the face of the Earth! A voice on the land! Until the amphibians came with their voices, the silence was broken only by the sound of rain on the rocks, or the rumble of thunder. Imagine how exciting it would have been to have heard the first sound ever to be made on the land!

Meanwhile the plants had left the sea. They grew in great variety and size, eating and making their own food with the air and sunlight. (point to the arboreal mosses and ferns in the Carboniferous Period)
The insects also came (point to the Insects in the Carboniferous Period), so there was food around for the amphibians.
They had a great time, they grew in different sizes and shapes. Unfortunately, they had one little problem: because of their skins, the amphibians needed to be near the

water to keep from drying out. Some wanted to be free of the water. They wanted to be independent, and to be able to travel! They wanted to be able to eat plants that grew farther from the water, but how? They thought and thought. They would have to leave the water! (Open up the Time Line of Life to the Permian Period)

So, gradually they developed a special kind of skin that did not dry out, and for their eggs they invented a shell. Now there was no problem! These were the reptiles. They had a skin that could be in the sun and shells for their eggs so they would not dry out. (point to the Permian Period reptile). Now they could move wherever they wished across the land! And then what happened? There were plenty of plants and amphibians. The reptiles had a good time and they grew and grew, many experiments were tried. There was no one to stop these creatures, and they became the lords and masters of the world! They took over the land, and the seas, and they even took control of the air!
(Open the Time Line of Life to the Mesozoic Era)
Here is a picture of one of these creatures: (Introduce the Diplodocus Chart)

Do you know how big this creature was? More than twenty meters long! This creature had a head that was a big as a man's body! Our classroom is 11 meters long. This animal would fill more than twice as this room like this! There was something peculiar about this creature. It had a brain in its head, and another down near the base of its tail, so that messages from the tail didn't have to travel all the way to the head and acted upon. Here is a picture of one of these creatures: (Introduce the Tyrannosaurus Chart)

Look at the head of this giant reptile. He was so big compared to the man. Can you imagine how the Earth must have shaken as these huge creatures stomped around, feeding? These animals had everything they wanted. The little animals had no chance against these big animals. And so the smaller fled to where it was cold, where the large reptiles could not live and could not get to them. As time went on, these animals who lived on the fringes where it was cold developed something to protect them from the cold. They developed hair or fur and a way to keep their blood warm without sunlight. These were the first birds and the mammals. (point to the Archaeopteryx of the Jurassic Period and to the Kangaroo of the Cretaceous Period) What about their eggs? They knew very well what happened to eggs that were left alone, so some began to carry them inside their bodies. The birds, however, could not carry their eggs and still fly, so they built nests for their eggs. One of the birds always stayed with the eggs until the babies were hatched, and fed them until they were big enough to leave the nest. (Open the Time Line of Life to the Cenozoic Era)
The mammals (point to the mammals of the Cenozoic Era) kept their eggs inside them and when the babies were born, they fed them with their own milk!

This was very new. Not all the creatures did this before so much! Mostly the other animals just left their eggs and some of the eggs were eaten by other animals. The young ones had to look after themselves. But the babies of the birds and mammals remained with their parents until they could take care of themselves.

The weather began to change again. It began to get colder and colder. The dinosaurs disappeared, though no one is really sure why this happened. Then the mammals took over. They grew and grew. They were able to go everywhere! There were giant animals: giant pigs. Giant hippopotami and giant elephants. (point to the large herbivore in the Oligocene Epoch)

The mammals had a good time, even as it got colder, and huge sheets of ice covered much of the Earth. The mammals moved all over the Earth in search of food and warmer weather. In the end, none of the giant mammals were able to survive, they died out.

Something very exciting happened toward the end of a very cold period. A completely new kind of creature emerged! It did not have sharp teeth to eat with, nor huge claws to fight with, nor fur. But it had something that none of the others had. It had a larger brain and it had the power to think and imagine. This creature also had an enormous amount of love. It was different from the other animals, because this animal could go beyond the love of its own children. It could love others, even others he/she would never see. This creature was the human being. (point to the human figure at the end of the time line)
You see, it was as if all of this (move your hand across the entire span of the Time Line
f Life) had to happen in order for man to come. Human beings would not have found
it possible to live if they would come here (point to the Cambrian Period), or when the plants were first trying out the land (point to the Silurian Period). At the end, though, everything was ready.

If the Earth had a voice, it would have said, "I have spread a thick carpet of grass for your feet so you can walk on soft ground. I have put flowers in my hair and covered myself with jewels. My cupboards are full of milk, meats, fruits, and vegetables for you to eat. Down in the cellars are coal and iron. Now that all is ready, it is time for you, to come."
Therefore, we are here. This (move your hand across the entire span of the Time Line
f Life) was all prepared for us, and now we are part of the story.
Key points of the “Story of life”
The story should not be too complete with all the names and facts. The children
have 6 years to discover more and more, independently or with the help of the
guide.
The timeline of life as well should not have all the names.
The story is not a purely factual account of the reality and it is not meant to put
forward any theory of evolution.
The story it is not a list of animals linked between each other.
There is an interplay between the environment of the Earth and life. The story
conveys the idea that life came as a necessity in order to return order to the
creation.
The story places a very important emphasis on the link between the non-living
world and the living world.
The story should help children to understand that we human beings are part of
the Earth therefore part of the Universe.
All forms of life are related and come from the same ancestor: the bacteria.
Looking at the origins helps to understand the unity of things.
An unconscious or universal intelligence at work, an intelligence that drives life
to solve problems. (E.g. “So they decided to build a sack inside their body with
water in it so that when there was no water they could still breathe.”)
The milestones in the “Story of life”
The first milestone
The beginning of life – unicellular life appearing as a response to
a necessity
The laws of the unicellular life: eat, grow, reproduce
Unicellular life becomes multicellular life
The specialization of cells: creatures with organs
Second milestone
The invasion of the land: plants, invertebrates(arthropods –
creatures with feet - insects) and only later
vertebrates(amphibians)
The evolution of the lungs – the beginning of the lungs
The evolution of the skin
The evolution of the eggs
Third milestone
Evolution of the hair/fur/feathers
Passage from the cold blood to warm blood – allows the
creatures to be active in lower temperatures
The parents take responsibility for the continuity of the species
(The birds that keep the eggs warm)
With the mammals they already gave birth to live babies and
some used their bodies to ensure the species
Fourth milestone
The arrival of the human beings
The human beings come with less physical abilities but with a
powerful mind to help them cope with the problems that arise
from having less physical abilities (E.g. build weapons, make clothes)
The love of the humans not only for their creeds but also for the
thers and for the universe that they are part of.
Practical points of telling the “Story of life”
The story should be given to all the children in the classroom, the most important is that all the young children 6 years old.
The story should be done in one sitting if possible.
After the story, the guide should stay with the children while they examine the time of life.
The guide should give the children time to reflect and do some follow-up work.
The timeline of life should not be out permanently unrolled.

The guide can talk about the classification of rocks:
Igneous rocks (recent rocks – some come from volcanic activity)
Sedimentary rocks (rocks originated from the sediments of other rocks)
Metamorphic rocks (rocks originated due to the pressure and heat but from other rocks)

Sedimentary rocks make up to 66% of the Earth’s crust, with 34 % being the igneous and the metamorphics. Igneous rocks however, forms the majority of 34 % (Ehlers and Blatt, 1997). The reason why sedimentary rocks account for most of the rocks on the Earth’s surface is because they are mainly found ocean floor basins which accounts to 70% of total area of the earth. The three rock types are further classified based on chemistry, environment of formation and how they are formed.

6 Kingdoms of Life
Archaebacteria

In 1983, scientists tool samples from a spot deep in the Pacific Ocean where hot gases and molten rock boiled into the ocean form the Earth’s interior. To their surprise they discovered unicellular (one cell) organisms in the samples. These organisms are today classified in the kingdom, Archaebacteria. Archaebacteria are found in extreme environments such as hot boiling water and thermal vents under conditions with no oxygen
r highly acid environments.
Eubacteria
Like archaebacteria, eubacteria are complex and single celled. Most bacteria are in the EUBACTERIA kingdom. They are the kinds found everywhere and are the ones people are most familiar with.
Fungi

Mushrooms, mold and mildew are all examples of organisms in the kingdom fungi. Most fungi are multicellular and consists of many complex cells. Fungi are organisms that biologists once confused with plants, however, unlike plants, fungi cannot make their own food. Most obtain their food from parts of plants that are decaying in the soil.
Protists

Slime molds and algae are protists. Sometimes they are called the odds and ends kingdom because its members are so different from one another. Protists include all microscopic organisms that are not bacteria, not animals, not plants and not fungi. Most protists are unicellular. You may be wondering why those protists are not classified in the Archaebacteria or Eubacteria kingdoms. It is because, unlike bacteria, protists are complex cells.
Plants

Plants are all multicellular and consist of complex cells. With over 250,000 species, the plant kingdom is the second largest kingdom. Plant species range from the tiny green mosses to giant trees. In addition plants are autotrophs, organisms that make their own food.
Animals

blocks.text: Today we have another story, but first let’s see if we can recall the story of life. Do you remember the Story of Life and the timeline of life? Do you remember at the end of the timeline of life there was a picture of a very special being? And who was that? Yes, us, the human beings. When you heard the story, you remember how we spoke about earth, and land and water settling down. Very early on we spoke about how there was a problem and there was trouble and life came to take care of the problem and purify the water. We also heard how life came to live on the land and how some animals became huge. And how with the amphibians came the first voice on the land. There were also the birds who could fly and build nests and some of them have beautiful voices to sing, and finally at last when the earth was ready there came human beings. Human beings like us. And then we looked at the long black strip and saw how long that strip was and how long it took to unroll and what did we see there at the very end? We saw the short amount of time that humans have been around in relation to the Earth. We saw that tiny white strip that tells us how long the human beings have been living here on Earth. What makes humans special? Thinking, loving, food, shelter and even the clothing. So today we want to think and talk about human beings and what makes us special (Doesn’t mean that other creatures and other life forms aren’t special. Human beings are special to other living beings, humans should realize that plants are rather special as well, but there are other things humans can do that
thers cannot)

In some ways the human beings are rather different than the animals that came before. You might think it is our body’s shape that is different. That is true, the human body is a little different. But that is not the only thing. The human mind is different. Let’s think about our minds. We can think of course, we use
ur mind for thinking. We can wonder, we can question, we can imagine, when

we tell a story you can wonder about what will come next, that is thinking. When human beings came to the Earth, they were thinking and wondering. They could see the sun, feel the warmth of the sun when it shined in the sky. They could see the sun’s journey through the sky during the day. They could see that the sun sank at the end of the day. They saw it rise again the next morning, and they could wonder about all of that. Where did the sun come from when it rose, and where did it go when it disappeared? Humans could think and wonder about the things they saw and how and why something happened. These early human beings could feel the wind, how it cooled them, when it was hot during the day. They could think and wonder where was the wind coming from? Where was it going? Early human begins thought about the rain, they could think about the how and the why about the rain. Why did it rain sometimes and no other times? And at night when looking at the heavens, the sky, they could see the stars and wonder about them. Humans made up stories about the sun and the wind, the rain and the stars. Sometimes we can find stories from long long ago that humans made up, stories that we can still listen to today. (Constellations – certain times of the year when they can be seen) Human beings could think, wonder, imagine, reason about how things happened the way they did. They could do all of this because of their special minds. We too, have that special mind. All of us have that special mind. There is also something else that made human beings different from other animals that came before them. Human beings can love in a special way. Of course, we love our parents and
ur brothers and sisters, children, friends, but you know what is so special about

human love is that apart from loving people we know, it is possible for us to love those who we don’t know. What do I mean about that? For example, we can love all the children in the world. This doesn’t mean we can hug them or kiss them, it means that we can wish them well and that no harm will come to them. This love means that we hope that none of them are cold or hungry or sick or unhappy. So, when we wish others well, we can think of that as love. Of course, we can also love can extend beyond human love. We love plants, animals, nature and our environment. When human beings came to the Earth, they came with abilities that other certain plants and animals were not able to do. Each kind of animal is given a special kind of life. Each animal lives according to a certain kind of pattern. It is almost as if the animal and a certain way of life belong together. This is also true for the different kinds of plants. Each animal for example eats what is special to its life. What do cows eat? Grass. They would never choose to eat anything other than grass. They even have special stomachs made so they can eat the grass. What do squirrels like to eat? Nuts, acorns and certainly not grass. Cows aren’t going to start eating nuts, are they? Certain birds like worms, or grains, or chickens eat anything they can find scratching around in the ground. But certainly, chickens don’t eat grass.

Earthworms eat the earth, they eat soil. Aren’t their bodies’ just ideal for living and eating the earth. If we look at the animal’s body maybe, we can get an idea what its life is life and what it likes to eat. What about human beings? Can I look at you and know what you like to eat? DO we all eat the same thing all the time? I eat many different things every week. What did you eat for breakfast? (Compare the differences between what the children eat). Did you have the same thing for lunch? What about dinner? We eat different things at different times. Imagine all the people all
ver the world just imagine what they are eating, we would be amazed at all

the different foods people are eating. That makes us very different! The variety of food is incredible! We can choose what we want to eat. Let’s think about our homes now. What kinds of homes do birds have? Nests! Parents build nests for their little ones. Certain birds build certain kinds of nests, the same kind of bird always build the same kind of nest. But what about us? Do we all live in the same kinds of houses? Some houses are made of wood, some are made of brick, some lives in apartments, and they are people who live in boats, houses on stilts, skyscrapers, farms. You would be very surprised by all the different kinds of homes people have lived in over the years. Let’s think of how we cover ourselves. Do animals keep the same covering? Animals with fur can shed fur and grow thicker fur when needed. They will always have fur or feathers, it will always have the same sort of covering. What about us? I’ve noticed you coming in wearing all different kinds of clothes in all sorts of colours. Do you agree? You are certainly not wearing the same clothes you wear in winter time and summer time. Human beings have many different forms of life when it comes to clothing, shelter, and what they eat. How is all of that possible? Because human beings have a special gift. The gift of hands! We use our hands to build things, to make things, and do things. We can make
ur own clothes and we can build our own homes, or we can find, grow, and

cook our food in all sorts of different ways. Stop and think about all the different things you do with your hands. It easy to take your hands for granted. Think about everything you did with your hands all day long until you go to bed. Humans came to the Earth with two legs to walk, so that left their hands were free for creating, working and doing things. Human beings came with three special gifts, special minds, special love, and special hands. All these special gifts together make humans special. I’ll tell you
ther stories about human beings. When you listen to them you can think of
these stories of human intelligence, human love and human work carried out by our hands.

Tell the story of the “Timeline of the hand”

blocks.text: Do you remember the story of the coming of the human beings? What did we speak about with the story of the human being? We were talking about how the human beings can think and imagine, how human beings love, we too love in the sense of – we can think kindly of other people that we don’t know – we hope that they are happy – we also love our world. Thinking, loving, in special ways are gifts given to the human beings that came to the earth with this gifts.

The humans came when the earth was prepared, the humans came when the earth was prepared for them to survive, there were vegetables, fruits, meat and fish for them to eat, the air was good for breathing, the sun kept them warm. The rain helped the plants grow, there was food and stone for the humans to make things so now with the help of this new timeline we can think of these human beings who lived a long time ago – human beings as us. We can think how they lived, how they survived.
[Start unrolling the timeline]

This is when human beings were first on earth, do you see the white marks, they help us understand all the years passing. With each white mark 100 000 years passed by. The marks help us to understand how much time passed. There are no pictures on the timeline, no pictures to tell us how the human beings were living and what they were doing, but they must have hunted and gathered plants, and in the winter they must’ve found shelter, ways to defend themselves from the cold and the other dangers. If they have not done all these things – they couldn’t survive.
[Stop at the hand]

But look now, what the humans used to do all the other things that I told you. It was the gift of the hands – this helped the human to satisfy their needs and survive. The hand is holding a stone, we can think of the hand holding a stone as representing the human work. The human use their mind and hand at all the times. If you look at the hand it has a stone, but not any stone but a stone that was specially prepared to be used as tool or weapon, an instrument of some kind. This special stone, it is not just a stone – we can call this one as a hand axe. This stone is like an extension of the hand. We can think of the tools made by the man as extensions of the human hand. All the timeline is black, like the night
we can’t see very well of what happened in that times. We can think of the

black as our lack of knowledge, our ignorance. What we find that from these long ago humans, it is not the remains of their bodies but it is the instruments that they used. With this instruments we try to understand how they lived. This long period of time from where we started to unroll the timeline, this is the Stone Age.

The disk of light that surrounds the hand we can think of it as a halo of light – we can regard the human hand as sacred. If we think of all the things that we can do with our hands it can seem that there is no end to what our hands can do. We can use our hand in other ways, not only for work, we can use our hand to express ourselves, to caress the others, to hold someone else’s hand. The hands satisfy not only the needs of the body but also the needs of the spirit. For a long period of time that hands not only working but doing all the things that the hands can do – they modified the environment in which the humans lived.
[Start unrolling the timeline]

Let’s think of the humans working, learning to defend themselves, cooking, doing shelter for themselves and many other things, but there was something for which the hands where not used: writing. Can you write?

Here is when the human beings started to write. Here is when they can record their beliefs, observations, feelings and daily life. The hands were working but not writing before this moment. There were no books, no newspaper, and no history books. The recorded history started here. With the written language we started to record the human story – our history. The people who devote themselves to write about history – they are called historians. They only study what’s represented here in the red part because there is nothing left from the human before this moment in time. The red strip is what it is our recorded history and because before they didn’t write it down, it is hard to know what they discovered, believed or thought. This red part represents the last 5000 or so years, here we find Sumerians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Egyptians, Aztecs, Greeks, Chinese, Indian and all the ancient civilizations. The black one doesn’t tell us too much about them.

Think back to the long black strip. It showed us what a short time the human begins have lived on our earth. If you think about the amount of time humans have lived in comparison to the Earth, it is so short it is just a blink of an eye. If we think of our own lifetime, our own human lifetime, it seems as though humans have been here a very long time, for millennia’s and millennia’s, for thousands and thousands of years. Almost everything before the red part, humans used tools of stone and tools of wood and they wandered over the land. This is a very long time before people settled down and before people started to live in cities. Before written language. Just imagine how many people during this long time how many people lived and died, lived and died, lived and died. Countless people. Many generations. We know they worked but we don’t know a lot about them. We don’t even have many bones. We do have stone instruments to tell us that they lived and worked and made life better for those that came after them. What did they leave in the end? They left everything that made civilization possible. All the unknown people that did not write left their technology, their art, their poetry, their religion, to the first civilization in histories that did have written language.

When we think about the first humans to invent writing about 5,000 years ago, we should think about all those before them who struggled in conditions that were so difficult and slowly made discovery after discovery and left to those who followed. They worked for themselves, but without knowing it, they also worked for us.

f the program and not at the beginning. Starting with the whole helps the
children to grow in a more opening minded ways, a more open hearted way. It can help with the prevention of the prejudice.

The children must grow appreciating what unites the human beings like this the children can grow more tolerant to appreciate the differences and diversity of the humanity on the planet Earth.

Story of Buddha by Pema Domingo: “Buddha was an Indian prince who had all kind of luxuries in his life but saw that although he had everything material in his life he still suffered. He also realized that everybody suffers so he had a strong determination of liberating himself from suffering to then help the rest. He left all his possessions and became having an ascetic life, meditating and having a few grains of rice per day. His body became weak and then realized that none of the extremes were right. He then started feeding himself properly and got enlightened. Buddha means literally ‘the awaken one’. He realized that in all things in life we need to practice what he called ‘the middle way’. We live in constant duality (beautiful/ugly, good/bad, attachment/rejection) and we have to perceive things just as they are ‘not too tight, not too loose’ freeing ourselves from judgment. Just accepting things as they are without getting attached neither rejecting. For this he discovered that there are certain tools, such as meditation to develop awareness in everything and help your mind to pay attention. Before he died he asked not to take what he said as a dogma. He said to please take his words, see if it makes sense in your life and if it does then apply it into your own life. That his teaching were the boat to get to the other shore but after getting there do not carry the boat with you. Although this is a philosophy of life there are many countries that do take it as a religion (Nepal, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Japan, China, North of India among others)”.

Presently came along a wolf, and knocked at the door, and said: “Little pig, little pig, let me come in.” To which the pig answered: “No, no, by the hair of my chiny chin chin.” The wolf then answered to that: “Then I’ll huff, and I’ll puff, and I’ll blow your house in.” So he huffed, and he puffed, and he blew his house in, and ate up the little pig. children.title: Presentation of the “The story of the Palaeolithic”

blocks.text: Do you remember when the human beings first came to the earth? Do you remember that we said that after a long period, the Earth has prepared herself for the human beings, prepared herself for this new kind of being. When the human beings finally came it was actually a rather difficult time on the earth, a rather difficult time for large parts of the earth. So all that long, long time ago when human beings first came a great part of the northern of the earth, was very very very cold. In fact for all the time that the human beings have been
n the earth it was a time when the ice came and went, came and went,

came and went. I said ice but you know what an ice age is, the ice time I am talking now, it is not the ice in the snow in the winter time. That ice lasted lasted and lasted like a terrible winter that went on for thousands of years. We can think of it as winter becoming colder and colder, snowing and snowing, never stopping in all the four seasons, so there were parts that never got warm. In the arctic, snow grew thicker and thicker, so gradually it transformed in great sheets of ice. And the sheets of ice become thicker and thicker and heavier and they began to move under their own weight. Sometimes this heavy ice sheets were 2000 m high, and the ice came further and further south. These giant sheets of ice acted as great bulldozers carving the continents and as they moved they destroyed what was in their way: trees, mountains and so on. As they came further and further south – what about the animals, they couldn’t live with that ice, they had to move away, but after a long period of time, the ice sheets started to melt. The water poured down on the sides of the mountains, rushed along the river beds, as the air become warmer and warmer – the ice retreated – the rivers would run and the oceans and lakes would rise again. With warmth and water the plants started to grow again, so came that the plants and the animals returned to what were the cold places. The places that were warm during the cold time, became very hot and the animals living there adapted to the hot weather. Since the human beings came to the earth, the ice came and went at least 4 times. These periods of the great ice are called ice ages and you can see them here.
[Unroll the timeline completely]

The ice ages are where we see the icicles and the last ice age was not that long ago. We can call these ice ages – glacial periods. We can call warm periods, the ones in between the icicles, interglacial periods. Some people call all of this time, the great ice age, the ice was not there all the time and not on all the earth. It is very difficult to find out how the humans lived during this period of time: we know that the humans came with special characteristics: a special love, the ability to use the hand, special mind and also they had each other. What the human beings didn’t have? They didn’t have fur or feathers, they were quite slow, they couldn’t jump too high, they were not “champions” at anything. From a physical point of view they were so
much weaker than the other animals. So the other animals could think about the humans as weak and helpless. [Go at the beginning of the timeline]

Look at the human beings here, they are really naked. But they live in a place where it is warm, they are naked but they are not feeling cold. If we look at the plants and the animals we can say that it is not that cold. Can you see that they are in a group? Are there any houses? Hmm, no cloths and no houses. There is a man cutting an animal, a woman collecting food from a bush and a man with a stone in his hand carrying a dead animal bring it back to this spot. Even if there is no house, this spot is a home base for these people – a place where you meet the others. Being in a group for them meant survival. Look at this man eating meat, I think that he is eating raw meat, not cooked meat. It doesn’t mean that he likes it like that, but many years ago they didn’t have fire so without fire they couldn’t cook: no clothes, no shelter, no cooked food, no supermarket, they had to look for their food hunt, gather it or scavenge – not an easy life. Definitely not easy but at least they are in a group, so they can
rganize themselves. Look at this man here, is chipping a stone, he is preparing

the stone tool, transforming a stone into a tool – a tool that will be used in the future, that requires in a special mind. To defend yourself, you would take something around yourself and use it to defend yourself – preparing it, makes the action far more special. He is trying to make the stone sharp to, use it as a hand axe.

What do we see up here? (A palm and other trees - during the ice age northern regions became very cold but in Africa it wasn’t that cold it was very dry.) Now we see the coming of the ice, are here any human beings? – Not in the pictures but they are there, hidden.

In this part you see something very special: fire. How does the fire appear in the nature: lightning or volcano eruption – but here we see the man with the fire, having the fire is like having the power of the gods. It is important to think about the power of the fire – the power of manipulating the fire. The humans learned how to keep the fire going, but not how to make it – they had to keep it always burning, take it with them wherever they went. Remember the man who was preparing tools, how was he doing it? Striking
ne stone towards the other (percussion) – and from that stones, some of them

made sparks, and they saws how a spark can start a fire – they understood how to make a fire. We don’t know exactly when they discovered it, later they discovered how to make fire by rubbing two pieces of wood. What did they use the fire for – for defending themselves and cook the food. That might happened from a mistake, someone dropping a piece of meat in the fire, and when they got it back, it was tasting different – it was tenderer. Using the fire to cook helped them to stay healthier and eat tenderer meat/vegetables. The discovery of the fire are so many. With the passage of time, the humans, made better tools, they specialized the tools so they can serve a certain purpose – which made them more efficient for cutting, making holes or digging. Let’s have a look at these two men? Are they cooperating? They are trying to keep that creature at a distance, they are working together – who would you rather be: a man with a stone or with a man

with a spear? But look, they are not naked anymore – they are covered with a fur – they wanted to feel more protected. To get the fur they needed special tools and use scrapers, they would chew it to make it soft – they needed that special scraper to take the skin from the hide. It took a lot of work, they first had the idea to get warm coats like the animals have. Human beings must’ve always lived in groups, they must’ve always cooperated. They are working like a team protecting themselves, if we want to cooperate, we need to communicate – we can use signs but mostly speech. We are not sure when speech came, but we are sure that at some point our ancestors became communicating through speech, it might seems like a new gift for the human being.
Look at this man preparing a tool, but it seems that he is using a mallet.

Let’s look at this group, they look very organized, they have a fire that they made, someone is coming back carrying a fish – they learned to catch fish – they are wearing clothes, they are bringing the food to the home base so it means that they share it. [The guide discusses a lit bit more about what’s going
n in the image]

Look a new ice age is coming, to escape this one they learned to shelter themselves in caves, using the fire to warm them up and to defend themselves from the animals. In that cold time, the animals were hungry and looking for food, but with the fire they could survive and keep the animals away.

These humans found shelter, they have weapons like spears and stones and the tools are getting smaller and smaller and more precise. Getting smaller tools, was very handy as they could make more tools from the same piece of stone, the tools are easier to carry, these people they even combined the stone and the wood to make a more powerful weapon.
Look here, what do you think that they are doing? They are burring this person
they are having a ceremony – they are going to cover him in a good bye

ritual. The fact that they take care of the person after he dies, he might think that there is life after death – this is the beginning of the spiritual needs, having beliefs and if you look carefully this man has a necklace – was it for religious purposes or maybe just vanity – we can’t know. What it is sure is that they took care of each other.

If we look at the next scene, we can see the people using the spears in a different way – they were fighting with an animal that looks like an elephant – was it an elephant – it was a mammoth. It took a lot of cooperation to defend
from such a big animal as the mammoth. Here we are in a period called the Stone Age, most of the tools were made of stone but not all – somewhere made of wood.
We can see up here that some of the tool were made of stone. The guide says that this period it is called Palaeolithic (from the Latin for Old stone).
Look at this people here, they are living in caves but also they are making their
wn kinds of huts. These huts were not permanent, just temporary but still are

an improvement. If we look at the clothes of the people in this epoch called the Upper Stone Age, we can see that some are sawn, they discovered how to make a needle and use it to make clothes adjusted to their body.

Look at all the people cooking over there, they are cooking fish – they have learned how to grill the fish on a stick. If you look at the man on the right, he is painting on the wall of the cave, during this time the Old Stone Age there are is a lot of cave art. No one knows why they painted, most of the paintings represent the animals. The paintings, most of them, are very deep in the cave, they might’ve been very important for the people there. Their live in the caves, it couldn’t been an easy life but if we compare them with the people who lived at the beginning of this timeline, they improved a lot. During all this time, they from the beginning until this point on the timeline, they had to hunt and gather fruits and plants – we can call these people: hunters and gatherers.
[Look back on the timeline and review]

If we look at the people here on the timeline, if we look at their tools, the skills that they’ve got (cooking, making fire, working the wood and stone), the art that they created, they are satisfying all their needs: spiritual and material. In these groups it existed a beginning of a specialization of work (some are cooking, some are fishing, some are making tools, some are making clothes or some are making paintings). In this time they might have exited people that learned and spent time investigating ways of helping the ones that are hurt or ill. People always used everything they could to make their life more comfortable and this is why we can see a change.

children.title: Story of the second timeline of the human beings – part 1

blocks.text: The guide says that today we are going to think of the human beings again. We will do this with the help of this timeline. We want to think of how the human beings lived and satisfied their needs from where we left with the other timeline.
The guide says that this timeline shows us the last 25 000 years, it is not that much compared with the other that was showing more than 500 000 years – so something is changed – the scale.
The guide invites the children to look at the beginning of the timeline and find
ut how the human beings were finding their food
The children says that the people hunted and gathered food.

The guide says that the people lived in groups, they had different customs, different tools, and in different places around the world – we can talk about different cultures. Do you remember that we couldn’t find out how they lived from their writings because they were not writing at that time. To learn more about them we had to dig and find different tools, artefacts and try to associate them with the different cultures. We know that they were human beings like us, just that they lived in a different period in time. Look at these people here, they are hunting a mammoth. In this time it was still cold, we can see it with our curved line and that must be right because the mammoths lived in a period with cold weather. Despite the fact that it is cold, the human beings found a way of life much better than a few thousand hundred years ago – they had new commodities, they developed new ways of hunting with traps. The people dug holes, covered them with leaves and when the animal felt in the pit they attacked it with spears. In that times, the humans used everything from an animal for food, clothes or building with the bones and skins – they even cracked open the bones of the animals and ate the marrow. The temperature is raising and the ice sheets are retreating and the world slowly becomes a warmer place. The mammoths have to follow the ice, but other animals move in, just like these horses here. The Solutrean people lived in the actual France. They had a very particular way
f hunting horses. They would make a lot of noise and scare the horses driving
them towards a cliff from where the horses would fall. In this place in France the scientists found so many horse bones that they think that this is what happened.

Let us look at this man here, what is he doing – he is making tools. His tool has the shape of a laurel leaf. Is that a tool or just an artefact for decoration? If we look at his neck he has a necklace. Some people think that the change of climate brought the horses north and when the temperature started to go even warmer, the horses and the people moved east. We don’t really know what happened to these people, some scientists say that maybe they went East with the horses and other say that some groups changed their habits. We can see here that they lived in caves, they made horse statues and that the vegetation in this place was of tundra. Here we find another civilization called the Magdalenians. They are famous for their extraordinary bone carving skills. This man has a harpoon like weapon for fishing in low waters.

The weather is getting warmer and warmer and the humans go towards North with the mammoths or head towards the water which had enough food. The woman in here is sawing – what did she need to saw – a needle. We already talked that they had great skills in bone carving and they could make needles from the bones. The vegetation changed as well changed with areas with steppe, pine forests and oaks. What about the mammoths, what is happening with them – some mammoths followed the cold weather, the humans hunted the ones remaining for food and soon the mammoths went extinct. The people living in the warm area next to the sea continued fishing, gathering molluscs and hunting smaller animals like wild pigs. But how do we know what they were eating? Well, sometimes, we find their garbage (kitchen madden)
and study what was in it – the term for madden comes from the Danish language as they were the first ones to use this method.

The people who used to live in a hunting and gathering manner, have to slowly change their habits. By this time, they already discovered how to make a bow and arrow for hunting, and they domesticated the wolves to protect themselves and to hunt.

Let us pass to the green period, it is a pressure for them to change how they live. It wasn’t everywhere around the world, but in some places. It is a transitional time from their hunting and gathering way of life to a new life. What kind of life, well that’s another story for another day.

children.title: Story of the second timeline of the human beings – part 2

blocks.text: On another occasion, the guide brings the timeline again and says that the planet was getting warmer and warmer so they had to change their life. The big animals were not around anymore and they had to hunt many small animals. Hunting the small animals it was a tendentious task as with each hunt there was less food to take back home. The humans had to find another way to gather food – let us imagine that moments a long time ago.

The humans are moving from cave to cave passing each season in another place, this is a laborious task even though they always return in the same places. At a certain time they bring back the animals and plants that they hunted and gathered. Some are rabbits, wild pigs and also seeds. They use the seeds to make food, and some might have fallen on the ground. Next year when they returned they saw the plants growing in their place – this might have repeated for a few times until someone came with the idea of scattering the seeds to grow the plants. They were planting seeds but also they were hunting and gathering.

We talked about how they started to grow plants, but what about the animals. Yes, we said that they used the domesticated wolf – the dog. They might’ve seen the wild sheep and goats in herds while they were hunting. Slowly they’ve learnt how to manage a heard and how to keep them close to the places where they lived. With the domesticated the animals the humans had to see if the animals breaded also in captivity – some animals would never
reproduce in captivity. With this discovery a new chapter of comfort has
pened for the human beings. Now they had no necessity to go and hunt, they

had skins for clothes, they discovered how to use the wool without killing the animals. Can you see any domesticated animals on the timeline? Look at the pigs here, the boy was a herded and in the background there are cows. With the big animals the humans discovered how to use them to work the land. They
are using tools to plough the soil. The first ploughs were used for pushing instead
f dragging. The humans started to do agriculture.

children.title: Story of the second timeline of the human beings – part 3 “Neolithic farmers”

blocks.text: The guide asks the children if the remember when we looked at this timeline and how people learned to grow plants instead of gathering them. Among the plants they learnt to grow they started to grow wheat. Instead of hunting animals they started to grow animals like pigs and sheep – they still hunted and gathered food only that not so much. Even now if you think well there are still people fishing or gathering leaves, however not so much as before. In some parts of the world there are still people who prefer hunting and gathering instead of rising their own animals. As we can see on the timeline, the weather got warmer and warmer and more people started doing agriculture. This change in how they obtained their food was as well a change in the way they lived. They were still Stone Age farmers but a new king of Stone Age farmers. We call it Stone Age as at that time they never used metal for their tools. Many of their tolls were made out stone, bone
r even wood. You see, with agriculture the people had to stay where their
crops and animals were, slowly growing into villages.

They had to clear the lands and slowly we could see the human beings transforming the environment in a way never seen before. If we look on the timeline we can see the word “agriculture” written here. Some people say that we can call this time the Agricultural revolution – revolution in the sense of an important change, but we must not confuse it with something happening fast, as it took a long time.

The people started to build houses meant to last. Now they didn’t have to move around so their houses had to be strong to last for years. Some of the houses were made of mud, some of stone, some of wood and some of a mixture of all these materials. Living in communities it meant that the people had to collaborate and help each other build their houses, take care of their crops and animals.

The humans living in that time used to have quarries to take the stone from. They used the stone not only for their houses or agriculture but also to satisfy their spiritual needs by building places for the gods. If we look on the timeline we can see the people building something here, there are lifting the stones to create the Stonehenge – it was one of the many places like this around the world – “henge” means circle.
This humans worked together sometimes for generations building these monuments. It might not look a lot for us today, but for these humans it was a grand work.

There are also other interesting constructions, called passage graves. What it is interesting about these monuments is that many are aligned with the Sun – this tells us that the monuments were very important for them.

With working together, special bonds between the people in the community were created. Thinking back of that monuments, this tells us how important the seasons for the agriculture were and therefore for the people living there. The

farmers after trying agriculture for many years they discovered that they produced more food that they required. This opened a new way of life in their communities in which not everyone had to produce food – they could exchange it for other commodities.

You can leave the clay to dry in the sun after you made it, however it must stay a long time so these humans thought that placing it close to the fire it is going to dry it fast – so they made special ovens for the pottery. Some say that the potters were also the first ones to have made something like a wheel, but who really knows it – maybe you can check and see what you can find.
The communities started to grow, some had around 150 people and this allowed them to do more work, to build things, to prepare the food, take care
f the animals. When they worked together, many families, like when building

The humans lived on the land but some felt safer on the water so they built lake dwellings – this helped them to stay safe and preserve their food.

With staying in one place, the possession started to accumulate and gather more importance in these people’s lives. For example can you see this woman here, you see she is using these stones to make something – what is she doing
she is grinding seeds – milling to make flour. Moving around with this kind of
tools it was impossible – it is a quern.

Today we still find people who move around with their animals, spending three months in one place – where are they living – maybe you can investigate more. I will just say that these people are called nomads and their way of life nomadic life.

Going back to the people settled, their lives had changed and they started to specialize: some were tool makers, some were masons, some spent time taking care of the spiritual life of the people: the priest, and some villages had even their chiefs.

children.title: Story of the second timeline of the human beings – part 4 “From the Neolithic to the urban life”

blocks.text: The guide on another day says that this another episode of the human story. The people changed their lives from a nomad life to a steady life with all that it came with it: the farming, the specializations and the cooperation. The communities where they lived started to grow becoming villages, then towns and cities. The people inspired each other when they lived together, the inventions started to come more quickly. At some point someone discovered that a soft substance came out a rock when it came close to a fire. In this way the people discovered that there is another type of stone. For thousands and thousands of years the people used the hardest stones to make their tools but now from that soft substance coming from a stone when it cooled down it was really strong. These were specials stones, they discovered that they could make tools from these special stones. Today we know that these were not stones, that was copper. And copper is a metal not a stone. Metal is less brittle than a stone, you can shape it with the fire and you can hammer it to change its shape. The people besides discovering the copper, also found that the copper came in an ore and they had to extract it with the help of the fire. You can see how important the fire is – they started working with the metal. This people were

called metal smiths. Extracting the metal from an ore it is called smelting and it was thinking that it was first done using a potter’s kiln (oven). Once the copper is purely extracted, when it is hot it is poured into a mould. With this the humans entered a new age, the age of metal.

They discovered that with using metal, if they mixed the metals (1 part tin, 9 parts copper) they created alloys that were harder and could be used with for building weapons. One of this alloys was bronze – so we can think of this moment really that we are in the Metal Age.

When the people discovered the iron, they had first to pass the first challenge: its high temperature to melt. Once this problem was solved, it replaced the bronze and became very popular as it was easier to find. The metal had to be heated, hit with a hammer to remove the bad bits, hammering it into place – this was called forging.

Iron was so important that the people wore it as jewellery. The smiths tried to keep it as a secret at the beginning but it did not last long as it soon became popular everywhere and brought a lot of comfort for everyone using it. The farmers started to use it to for their tools, some people became iron sellers – or merchants. The tools used for farming could be used also for war. So in the age
f metal, as people accumulated possessions, we see that the people started
to defend their communities – we can think of this picture as a palisade.
The humans started to build as high as they could, building iron age forts – buildings for living and defending themselves.

The population kept growing and growing, the people needed more land, so they had to clear it for the agriculture. Iron implements were also used for cleaning lands, so more villages became towns and more towns became cities. When they cleared land they had to cut down trees and you see, having metal tools was of great help.

The biggest cities of that times were in Mesopotamia and one of them was called Uruk with 80 000 people living there. With the coming of towns and cities, the scribes appeared and the soldiers for defence.

We talked a lot about food, when we talked about hunting and gathering or farming – it is also about food. The large cities required food, the people living in the villages could trade it with them in exchange for clothing or tools. The clothes became every time more sophisticated, for the yarn they had to take the wool and spin it into yarn, for linen they had to use flax. After getting the thread, they had to weave it to make the fabric and from the fabric they had to make the clothes. As the people looked for more and more clothes, the farmers started to bread their sheep for the wool – special sheep for getting the best wool.

This first cities flourished, there were many civilizations and their traces we can see them for example with the Great Pyramid. This is one of the 7 ancient world wonders – the only one still here. Do you know the other six?

Civilization did bring many important inventions: like writing and the numbers. Civilization, the numbers and the written language are very tied together. These inventions were crucial for the organization of the society, payment of the taxes, writing their stories and traditions. With the written language we can know what they thought and how their life was.

The people passed from agriculture to horticulture. The ancient civilization developed on the banks of the rivers like you might already heard, Mesopotamia, in between the rivers. This was due to the good soil for agriculture and the supply for water. We can think of these civilizations as the river civilizations. Water is an essential element for the life, be it plants, animals and humans. Rivers became important for commerce and the civilizations well connected with rivers developed and commerce flourished.
Let us look here at the Trojan War, we are back in the Bronze age. The Trojan War is described in the Greek mythology. It was one of the stories passed by
ral language. This story got also to the ears of a famous Greek blind poet

called Homer. He wrote a poem “The Iliad” and the people who read the poem thought that this was just a myth. The Iliad it is not only a myth and we know that because a German archaeologist excavated and found the remains of 9 cities, one on top each other. He found the remains of the city of Troy.

This was a long time ago, the Greeks kept first the story alive and later it was passed to written language. During the time it was told from mouth to mouth, the story changed. This story it is important because it symbolizes the beginnings
f the European literature, literature comes from the Latin word for letter.

When we look back on this timeline what we can see is that we were hunters and gatherers for such a long time, but when farming appeared we fast moved to an urban style of life and with the urban life we can talk about civilization. With the civilization we started to specialize our work, we developed, discovered and invented advancing and growing faster than at any time before.
The most important thing it is that as we grew in numbers and with the specialization of work we became more dependent on the others.

What we see in this story, a story of societies becoming more and more complex, however we should always remember that we depend on the farmers and the food they provide. The farmers depend on the rivers and there we go a circle of interdependencies that we need to appreciate and respect.

Laetoli is a site in Tanzania, dated to the Plio-Pleistocene and famous for its hominin footprints, preserved in volcanic ash. The site of the Laetoli footprints (Site G) is located 45 km south of Olduvai Gorge. The location and tracks were discovered by archaeologist Mary Leakey and her team in 1976, and were excavated by 1978. Based on analysis of the footfall impressions "The Laetoli Footprints" provided convincing evidence for the theory of bipedalism in Pliocene hominins and received significant recognition by scientists and the public. Since 1998, paleontological expeditions have continued under the leadership of Amandus Kwekason of the National Museum of Tanzania and Terry Harrison of New York University, leading to the recovery of more than a dozen new hominin finds, as well as a comprehensive reconstruction of the paleoecology. Dated to 3.7 million years ago, they were the oldest known evidence of hominin bipedalism at that time. Subsequently, older Ardipithecus ramidus fossils were found with features that suggest bipedalism. With the footprints there were other discoveries excavated at Laetoli including hominin and animal skeletal remains. Analysis of the footprints and skeletal structure showed clear evidence that bipedalism preceded enlarged brains in hominins. At a species level, the identity of the hominins who made the trace is difficult to construe precisely; Australopithecus afarensis is the species most commonly proposed.

The history of calendars, means that people creating and using methods for keeping track of days and larger divisions of time, covers a practice with ancient roots. Archeologists have reconstructed methods of timekeeping that go back to prehistoric times at least as old as the Neolithic. The natural units for timekeeping used by most historical societies are the day, the solar year and the lunation. Calendars are explicit schemes used for timekeeping. The first historically attested and formulized calendars date to the Bronze Age, dependent on the development of writing in the Ancient Near East. The Sumerian calendar was the earliest, followed by the Egyptian, Assyrian and Elamite calendars. A larger number of calendar systems of the ancient Near East appear in the Iron Age archaeological record, based on the Assyrian and Babylonian calendars. This includes the calendar of the Persian Empire, which in turn gave rise to the Zoroastrian calendar as well as the Hebrew calendar. Calendars in antiquity were usually lunisolar, depending on the introduction of intercalary months to align the solar and the lunar years. This was mostly based
n observation, but there may have been early attempts to model the pattern
f intercalation algorithmically, as evidenced in the fragmentary 2nd-century

Coligny calendar. Nevertheless, the Roman calendar contained very ancient remnants of a pre-Etruscan 10-month solar year. The Roman calendar was reformed by Julius Caesar in 45 BCE. The Julian calendar was no longer dependent on the observation of the new moon but simply followed an algorithm of introducing a leap day every four years. This created a dissociation of the calendar month from the lunation. In the 11th century in Persia, a calendar reform led by Khayyam was announced in 1079, when the length of the year was measured as 365.24219858156 days. Given that the length of the year is changing in the sixth decimal place over a person's lifetime, this is outstandingly accurate. For comparison the length of the year at the end of the 19th century was 365.242196 days, while today it is 365.242190 days. The Gregorian calendar was introduced as a refinement of the Julian calendar in 1582, and is today in worldwide use as the de facto calendar for secular purposes.
